reason: axe could not decide because the elements overlap others, and both probes came back incomplete, so I read the computed colors. On cards.budget-edit the +4 avatar counter has an opaque fill (white under a 16% tint, rendering rgb(232,233,238)) behind rgb(54,54,68) text: 9.8:1 against 4.5:1. On invoicing.row-selected the 1 item selected text sits on the bulk bar's solid white: 11.9:1. Neither background has a darker part under the text.

The backward jump is scrolling, not order. Tab stop 14 (This budget ends) sits at y 739 inside the form's scroll area and stop 15 (Additional options) at y 844, so the order runs forward. Focus scrolled the area from 23 to 256 px, which is why the second stop shows higher in the viewport (772 then 644).

After Save changes, the last stop of the left form pane, Tab moves to the avatar stack in the preview pane on the right, which sits higher on screen. The preview follows the form in the DOM, so the order is left column then right column and every control stays reachable.
criterionAnalysis: 2.4.3 asks for an order that keeps meaning and operability. Tab walks the form top to bottom, then Cancel and Save changes, then the read-only preview pane, then Close: the two columns in reading order. 1.3.2 asks for a meaningful sequence, and the DOM sequence matches the visual left-to-right layout. The upward move on screen is a column change, not a skipped or misordered control. No other A or AA criterion covers it.

reason: The Figma option is a tag chip with tabindex -1, so Tab skips it by design. From the Allowed merchants input, ArrowLeft and ArrowRight move focus across GitHub, Figma, Notion and Slack, and Figma shows a focus ring when it is reached. Each chip's description reads Press Delete or Backspace to remove, so the chip has a keyboard path.

The Open combobox menu button has tabindex -1, so Tab skips it. The combobox input beside it takes focus with Tab and opens the same menu with ArrowDown, on both cards.budget-edit (Spend controls) and the Add job title dialog. The button duplicates a control that works from the keyboard.
criterionAnalysis: 2.1.1 asks that all functionality work from a keyboard. Opening the menu does: Tab to the combobox input and press ArrowDown, and aria-expanded turns true and the options show on both sampled states (screenshots cards.budget-edit-spendcontrols-arrowdown.png and settings.add-job-title-arrowdown.png). The disclosure button is a pointer shortcut kept out of the tab order, as in the ARIA APG combobox pattern, and screen reader users can still activate it. 4.1.2 passes: the button has a name and exposes expanded and haspopup. No A or AA criterion fails.

reason: The Allowed merchants listbox is a zero-size, position:fixed live region (aria-live polite) that owns the four chips through aria-owns. It is not a control and has no handler of its own; the check flagged it because an ancestor has a click handler. The chips it owns take focus with the arrow keys from the input.

The Category combobox carries autocomplete=garbage, a made-up token that keeps browsers from filling it. The field picks a budget or transaction category (Software, Venue Rental) and collects nothing about the user.

value.description: We’ll automatically assign this category to transactions in this budget.
value.name: Category
value.template: combobox "Category" [expanded=false, haspopup=listbox] (We’ll automatically assign this category to transactions in this budget.)

criterionAnalysis: 1.3.5 covers fields that collect information about the user and serve one of the 53 input purposes it lists, such as name, email, address or card number. Category is not one of them and holds no personal data, so the criterion does not apply. The invalid token is real, but there is no user-data purpose for a browser or assistive tool to expose. No other A or AA criterion covers an autocomplete value.
